title: Industry Nine Revive 2.0 Wheelset Review – spencer harding
content:
With Industry Nine‘s acquisition of We Are One, the Asheville, North Carolina-based company can keep the entire wheel manufacturing process in North America. The product of this merger, along with many other wheel combinations, is the WR1 Revive 2.0 gravel rims featuring I9 Solix classic hubs. The rims feature WR1’s Convergence technology and the Solix hub’s continuously phased engagement, yielding 605 points of engagement or .59 degrees. See what Spencer thought about these tech-filled wheels below…

Not to beat a dead horse too many times, but wheel reviews are difficult. Ron Lewis did a splendid job speaking to the difficulty with an eloquence I can’t match in his review of the Teravail  Fluent wheels recently. Wheels, by design, disappear and aren’t a contact point akin to saddles, grips, bars, or pedals. Wheels connect us to the ground, but even then they are buffered by the endless permutations of tire choices. I will do my darndest to dissect these wheels, but these are really high-end, machined in the US hubs and Canadian-made carbon rims, and to none’s surprise, they are sweet. I still remember the joy when I got to ride/review my first set of carbon wheels, which happened to be the same pairing of WR1 and I9, though this was prior to the acquisition. Many of my thoughts ring true from that review; carbon wheels are still frickin’ sweet, and the freehub noise is, likewise, a bit much.

Industry Nine Revive 2.0 Wheelset Quick Hits

  • Revive 2.0 Rims
    • Material: Carbon
    • Size: 700c
    • Hole Count: 24h & 28h
    • Internal Width: 25mm
    • Rim Depth: 19mm
    • ERD: 602.5mm
    • Weight: 360g (24h & 28h)
  • Hubs: SOLiX J-Bend
    • P.O.E: 605 points
    • Engagement: .59 degrees
    • Mechanism: Continuously phased, 5-pawl x 121-tooth drive ring
    • Spoke System: Direct-thread machined aluminum for System hub or J-Bend Steel (reviewed) on classic scalloped hubs.
    • Bearing Spec: Equalized spec, full-contact endcap seals + proximity dust/water shield
    • Preload System: Bore-diameter contraction – eliminates play, maximizes longevity
  • $1899 as reviewed
  • Freehub options: Campy N3w, HG-11, Microspline-R, and XDR.
  • Hub shell colors: Black, Bronze, Gold, Orange, Purple, Red, and Silver (reviewed)
  • Available in standard 12 x 100/142 thru axle and 9 x 100/135 QR
  • Spokes: I9 System alloy, Sapim CX-Ray bladed (reviewed), and Sapim Race

Revive 2.0 Rims With Convergence Technology

The most aesthetically pleasing part of the Revive 2.0 rims is the convergence pattern of the spoke bed. Each spoke is offset +/- 6 degrees from flat to perfectly align the spoke head and nipple for each spoke. The back-and-forth sinuous luge of the rim bed is as elegant as it is practical. Also, gotta shout out the name Convergence in the context of the company’s name, We Are One. Convergence really ties the room together; well played.

If you have worked on wheels at all, you have probably seen nipples pull through rims or cracking around the spoke holes. Convergence creates “360-degree full contact” between the nipple and rim. We have seen offset spoke beads to keep spoke length equal between both sides of the rim, but I haven’t seen a rim truly equalize the point pressure at the nipple/rim interface. I have experienced zero issues with the Revive Rims during my testing period, so I’ll have to believe their claim for now.

Solix Hubs

Featuring I9’s continuously phased freehub mechanism shared with their Hydra2 hubs, the Solix hubs have 605 points of engagement, creating a .59 degree of engagement. While that is not technically instant, it’s pretty damn close. Basically, you are never going to feel any lull in the engagement of these hubs when you put the hammer down. The five pawls each have three small teeth per pawl that allow the first pawl to engage nearly instantly, allowing the subsequent pawls to progressively engage to catch the coming torque. The 121-tooth drive ring and pawls are spaced as such that there is almost always a pawl engaging, unless you can feel .59 degree of slop in your pedal stroke, which you surely can not.

The Solix hubs feature low drag via reduced pawl spring pressure, smaller drive ring diameter, and relocated freehub seals. The axle and bearing layout has been updated with equalized bearing spec and the best seals I9 has used.

Setup

Now the only, and I mean the only, issue I had with these wheels was the tubeless tape, which may or may not have been the manufacturer’s issue. These wheels came to me after Miguel had too much on his plate, and when I set them up, I found something curious I had never come across before. The tubeless tape for this 25mm rim was something like 15mm and wrapped twice, but once on each side of the rim bed. This left a seam right on the spoke holes and subsequently led to slow leaks.

Miguel could not recall if he had the rim locally retaped or if it was factory spec. I9 mentioned that this style may have been used in the past before their acquisition of WR1, but that a new tape was being implemented at the moment. A simple wrap of some fresh tape and zero issues since then. Whatever the oversight or issue was, it was easily rectified. Do you tape rims like this? Im sure someone in the comments will tell me this is superior for saving 3 grams and 2.75 watts at 23 kph or some shit.

Wheels Disappear but the Buzz Lingers

With great design, we hope it just disappears from our perception. The convergence rim tech and incredible engineering of the I9 hubs mean I just forget about my wheels; they work flawlessly. The only reminder of all that tech, research, and machining is the damned freehub noise. I9 has toned down their freehub noise since the initial Hydra hubs, but the insane engagement of the Solix hubs comes with buzzing. Occasionally I’ll find myself becoming accustomed to the noise, but if I am on a downhill with friends, they tend to chide me about the noise.

I don’t know if I need absolutely silent Onyx hubs. My last foray into quieter pawls on WTB hubs led me down a rabbit hole of chasing every rattling zip tie or housing on my bike. The Solix hubs exist not as an absolute outlier in terms of buzz, but definitely far from the center. I think we have superseded the need to have loud hubs as a signifier of quality, or of just how impressive the engagement of your hubs is. I9, can we get quieter hubs just as exquisitely engineered as your loud hubs one day?

Warranty

When I encourage people to get carbon rims, it is usually after they have destroyed other rims, hubs, or just whole wheels. At that point, they need a warranty for their abusive riding. So, to that point, I find that above any engagement spec or weather seal, it is the warranty on the product I am curious about. I9 has a great warranty that includes:

  • Carbon Rims are covered for life against defects in material or workmanship, and impact damage while riding within the intended use of the wheel
    • They offer rim replacement or a factory rebuild for $100-125
  • Hubs are covered for five years against defects in material or workmanship.
    • For the first two years, coverage includes parts, labor, and return shipping. From years three through five, parts are covered, but labor and shipping are not. Bearings and other normal wear items are excluded

I didn’t get to test the warranty on this review, but the warranty is pretty damned comprehensive.

Conclusion

I have very much enjoyed my time on the Revive 2.0 rims. Minus the tape issue, the experience has been without fault. After many months of hard riding from rough pavement to low-class singletrack, the rims only show the slightest deviation from true, an amount I’d scarcely fix even if they happened to be rim brake wheels. My initial time with an incredibly high engagement I9 hub was on a mountain bike wheelset where the near-instantaneous engagement felt more necessary in techy rock sections. Being far from a performance gravel or road rider, that level of quick engagement felt unnecessary for my style of riding, but I’ll be damned if it wasn’t sweet. If you want to support domestic manufacturing, demand high engagement hubs, love anodized color options, and want impressively handcrafted carbon rims, the I9 Revive 2.0 wheelset might just be for you.

Pros

  • Lightweight carbon rims are fucking sweet
  • Near-instant engagement with Solix hubs
  • Lifetime warranty on rims
  • 5-year warranty on hubs
  • Convergence rim technology is as elegant as it is well engineered
  • Hubs (Asheville, NC) and Rims (Kamloops, BC) are North American-made

Cons

  • 25mm internal feels safe at the moment but behind the ever-wider tire trend in gravel
  • Only 24h and 28h rim options may leave folks accustomed to more spokes spooked; let the warranty soothe your concerns
  • Stock tape was an issue, but I9 has changed their tape in the interim
  • .59 degree engagement feels superfluous for gravel
  • Loud freehub noise can be distracting

See more at Industry Nine.
